mainTopic: Washing and design of the בגדי כהונה, and how each garment atones for a specific sin
overview: The amud opens by finishing a ברייתא about washing the בגדי כהונה. Very dirty garments may not be washed at all, and a second view says they are never washed, because אין עניות במקום עשירות. Next, a ברייתא describes the כהן גדול's מעיל: it was all תכלת, with woven pomegranates and golden bells on its hem. One view counts 72 bells and the other counts 36, and רבי עינייני בר ששון points out that the same 36-versus-72 dispute appears about the shades of נגעים. He also teaches that the בגדי כהונה bring atonement just as קרבנות do. He then matches each of the eight garments to a specific sin. The גמרא challenges this from רבי יהושע בן לוי, who says bloodshed is atoned for by the עגלה ערופה and לשון הרע by the קטרת. The גמרא answers by splitting the cases. The כתונת atones for a known killer who acted on purpose without a warning, and the עגלה ערופה atones when the killer is unknown. The קטרת atones for private לשון הרע, and the מעיל atones for public לשון הרע. The amud ends with the הדרן closing פרק המזבח מקדש.

steps.title: Very dirty garments may not be washed
steps.stepSummary: If the בגדי כהונה got so dirty that they would need strong cleaners, they may not be washed even with plain water.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the garments got so dirty that they would need natron or soap, you may not wash them even with water.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a ruling about washing the כהנים's garments. If they are very dirty, they cannot be washed at all, not even with water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling sets a limit. Garments with light dirt might be washed with water. Once the dirt is bad enough to need strong cleaners like נתר and אהל, the garment is past the point of washing, and even water is not allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: a kind of soap or cleaning plant

phrases.english: If they reached the point of needing natron and soap,
one may not launder them, even with water.

steps.triggerLanguage: הוּגְּעוּ לְנֶתֶר וְאָהָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a ברייתא that began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Garments dirty enough to need strong cleaners may not be washed, even with water.

steps.title: A stricter view: never wash them
steps.stepSummary: יש אומרים: the garments may never be washed, because a poor man's fix does not belong in a place of wealth.
steps.simpleTranslation: And some say: You may not wash them at all, because there is no poverty in a place of wealth.
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion says the בגדי כהונה may never be washed, even if they are only a little dirty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 1 allowed washing light dirt. This view forbids washing completely. Its reason is that washing and reusing clothes is what poor people do, and the בית המקדש is a place of wealth, so only fresh, new-looking garments fit there.

keyTerms.meaning: there is no poverty in a place of wealth

steps.whatToRemember: There are two views on washing בגדי כהונה. The first allows washing light dirt with water only. The יש אומרים forbid washing entirely, because of אין עניות במקום עשירות.
steps.whyThisMatters: The principle אין עניות במקום עשירות shows that the honor of the מקדש requires a richer standard than ordinary life.

phrases.english: And some say:
One may not launder them at all,
because there is no poverty in a place of wealth.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְיֵשׁ אוֹמְרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a stricter opinion than step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The garments are never washed, because of אין עניות במקום עשירות.

steps.title: The robe was entirely sky-blue
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that the כהן גדול's מעיל was made completely of תכלת, based on a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: The robe was entirely of sky-blue wool, as it says: 'And he made the robe of the ephod, all of sky-blue.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new ברייתא about the כהן גדול's robe and says it was all תכלת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The source is the פסוק's words כליל תכלת, 'completely sky-blue.' This sets up the next question, because the hem had other colors, so the ברייתא must explain how the hem was made.

keyTerms.meaning: the robe of the כהן גדול

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
The robe was made entirely of sky-blue wool,
as it is stated:
"And he made the robe of the ephod, all of sky-blue wool."
phrases.notes: שמות 39:22

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מְעִיל כּוּלּוֹ שֶׁל תְּכֵלֶת הָיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the design of the מעיל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מעיל was made entirely of תכלת, learned from כליל תכלת.

steps.title: How was the hem made?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks how the hem (שוליים) of the robe was made.
steps.simpleTranslation: Its hem: how was it made?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks a question to set up its description of the robe's hem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The robe itself was all תכלת, but the תורה describes pomegranates and bells on the hem. The ברייתא now asks how that hem decoration was made.

phrases.english: Its hem, how was it made?
phrases.notes: The פסוק says they made pomegranates on the hem of the robe (שמות 39:24).

steps.triggerLanguage: שׁוּלָיו כֵּיצַד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the body of the robe to its hem.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the pomegranate decorations on the hem were made.

steps.title: Woven pomegranates on the hem
steps.stepSummary: Three colors of wool are twisted together and shaped like closed pomegranates, or like the pointed tops of children's helmets.
steps.simpleTranslation: He takes sky-blue, purple, and scarlet wool twisted together and shapes them like pomegranates that have not opened, like the cone-tips of helmets on children's heads.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers step 4 and explains what the pomegranates on the hem looked like.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pomegranates were made from three twisted colors: תכלת, ארגמן and תולעת שני. They were shaped like unripe pomegranates whose tops have not opened yet, which look like the pointed tip of a child's cap.

keyTerms.meaning: cone-shaped tips of helmets or caps

phrases.english: He brings sky-blue wool and purple wool
and scarlet wool, twisted together,
and makes them like pomegranates
that have not opened their mouths,
phrases.notes: Picture an unripe pomegranate whose little crown on top is still closed.

phrases.english: and like the cone-tips of helmets
that are on the heads of children.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵבִיא תְּכֵלֶת וְאַרְגָּמָן וְתוֹלַעַת שָׁנִי שְׁזוּרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The pomegranates were made of three twisted colors and shaped like closed pomegranates or the cone-tips of children's caps.

steps.title: Seventy-two bells on the hem
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says 72 golden bells with 72 clappers were hung on the hem, 36 on each side.
steps.simpleTranslation: He brings seventy-two bells with seventy-two clappers inside them, and hangs thirty-six on one side and thirty-six on the other side.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues describing the hem and says how many bells hung on it: 72 in all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each bell (זוג) had its own clapper (ענבל) inside, so there were 72 of each. They were split evenly, 36 on each side of the robe. This is the first opinion, and the next step gives a different number.

phrases.english: And he brings seventy-two bells
that have inside them seventy-two clappers,

phrases.aramaic: וְתוֹלֶה בָּהֶן שְׁלֹשִׁים וְשִׁשָּׁה בְּצַד זֶה
phrases.english: and he hangs them, thirty-six on this side
and thirty-six on that side.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמֵבִיא שִׁבְעִים וּשְׁנַיִם זַגִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the bells to the description of the hem.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There were 72 bells on the hem, 36 on each side.

steps.title: Another view: only thirty-six bells
steps.stepSummary: רבי דוסא in the name of רבי יהודה says there were only 36 bells, 18 on each side.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי דוסא says in the name of רבי יהודה: There were thirty-six, eighteen on this side and eighteen on that side.
steps.whatsHappening: A second תנא disagrees with step 6 and says there were half as many bells.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The disagreement is only about the number. The first opinion says 72 bells, 36 per side, and רבי דוסא says 36 bells, 18 per side. Both agree the bells were split evenly between the two sides.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי דּוֹסָא אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יְהוּדָה:
phrases.english: Rabbi Dosa says in the name of Rabbi Yehuda:
There were thirty-six:
eighteen on this side
and eighteen on that side.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי דּוֹסָא אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the number of bells in step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There were 36 bells, 18 on each side.

steps.title: The same numbers appear in a dispute about נגעים
steps.stepSummary: רבי עינייני בר ששון says the 72-versus-36 dispute here matches a dispute about the shades of נגעים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עינייני בר ששון said: Just like the dispute here, so is the dispute about the shades of נגעים.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא notices that the bell dispute has a twin: a dispute about how many shades of נגעים there are. This sets up the proof in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He is not deciding who is right about the bells. He is pointing out a parallel: in both places, one opinion says 36 and the other says 72.

keyTerms.meaning: the shades or appearances of צרעת marks

phrases.english: Rabbi Inini bar Sason said:
Just as there is a dispute here,
so there is a dispute about the shades of leprous marks,

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּמַחְלוֹקֶת כָּאן כָּךְ מַחְלוֹקֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares the bell dispute to another dispute with the same numbers.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The dispute over 72 or 36 bells parallels the dispute over the number of shades of נגעים.

steps.title: The משנה about the shades of נגעים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה: רבי דוסא בן הרכינס says there are 36 shades, and עקביא בן מהללאל says 72.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: The shades of נגעים: רבי דוסא בן הרכינס says thirty-six, and עקביא בן מהללאל says seventy-two.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up step 8 by quoting the משנה that shows the same 36-versus-72 dispute about נגעים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The quote proves the parallel is real. Again one side says 36 and the other says 72. In both disputes, a רבי דוסא holds the smaller number.

keyTerms.meaning: a תנא who holds there are 36 shades

steps.whatToRemember: The bell count (72 or 36) and the count of shades of נגעים (72 or 36) are disputed with the same pair of numbers.
steps.confusionAlert: Two different people named רבי דוסא appear here. The one in the bell dispute speaks in the name of רבי יהודה. The one in the נגעים משנה is רבי דוסא בן הרכינס. Don't assume they are the same person.

phrases.english: As we learned in a mishna: The shades of leprous marks:
phrases.notes: This משנה is in נגעים 1:4.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי דּוֹסָא בֶּן הַרְכִּינָס אוֹמֵר: שְׁלֹשִׁים וְשִׁשָּׁה,
phrases.english: Rabbi Dosa ben Harkinas says: thirty-six;

phrases.aramaic: עֲקַבְיָא בֶּן מַהֲלַלְאֵל אוֹמֵר: שִׁבְעִים וּשְׁנַיִם.
phrases.english: Akavya ben Mahalalel says: seventy-two.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן: מַרְאוֹת נְגָעִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the source that supports step 8's comparison.
steps.raayaObject: That a dispute over 36 versus 72 exists regarding the shades of נגעים.

steps.title: Why offerings sit next to priestly garments in the Torah
steps.stepSummary: רבי עינייני בר ששון says the Torah put the section on קרבנות next to the section on בגדי כהונה. This teaches that the garments bring atonement, just as קרבנות do.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי עינייני בר ששון said: Why was the section about offerings placed next to the section about the priestly garments? To teach you: just as offerings bring atonement, so too the priestly garments bring atonement.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching from the same רבי עינייני בר ששון we just saw in step 8. Here he explains why two sections of the Torah sit side by side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When two Torah sections are placed next to each other, we learn something from one about the other. Here we learn that the בגדי כהונה have the same power as קרבנות: they bring כפרה. This sets up the list of garments that follows.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the opening principle for the whole list. Every garment that follows is explained as atoning for a particular sin.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Inini bar Sason said:
Why was the section of offerings placed next
to the section of the priestly garments?
To tell you:
just as offerings bring atonement,
so too priestly garments bring atonement.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָמָּה נִסְמְכָה פָּרָשַׁת קׇרְבָּנוֹת לְפָרָשַׁת בִּגְדֵי כְהוּנָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a second, separate teaching from the sage of step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The בגדי כהונה bring atonement, just as קרבנות do.

steps.title: The tunic atones for bloodshed
steps.stepSummary: The כתונת atones for שפיכות דמים. The proof is the story of יוסף's brothers, who dipped his tunic in blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: The tunic atones for bloodshed, as it says: 'And they slaughtered a goat and dipped the tunic in the blood.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is the first garment on the list. The tunic is matched to the sin of murder.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The link comes from a פסוק in which a tunic and blood appear together. The brothers had plotted to kill יוסף. The tunic is therefore tied to the sin of bloodshed.

keyTerms.meaning: the tunic, the long inner garment of a כהן

phrases.english: The tunic atones for bloodshed,
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets; the word in square brackets is the corrected wording. The meaning is the same.

phrases.english: as it says: "And they slaughtered a goat,
phrases.notes: בראשית 37:31, about יוסף's brothers.

phrases.english: and dipped the tunic in the blood."

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּתוֹנֶת מְכַפֶּרֶת עַל שְׁפִיכוּת דָּמִים שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins applying the principle of step 10 to each garment.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כתונת atones for שפיכות דמים.

steps.title: The trousers atone for forbidden relations
steps.stepSummary: The מכנסיים atone for גילוי עריות. The פסוק itself says the trousers are made to cover nakedness.
steps.simpleTranslation: The trousers atone for forbidden relations, as it says: 'And make for them linen trousers to cover the flesh of nakedness.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is the second garment. The trousers are matched to sins of immorality.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof is direct. The Torah says the trousers exist to cover ערוה, nakedness. A garment whose job is modesty atones for sins of immodesty.

phrases.english: The trousers atone for forbidden relations,
as it says: "And make for them linen trousers
phrases.notes: שמות 28:42.

phrases.english: to cover the flesh of nakedness."
phrases.notes: The square-bracket words finish the פסוק. Some versions leave out the round-bracket word את.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכְנָסַיִם מְכַפֶּרֶת עַל גִּילּוּי עֲרָיוֹת שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next garment on the list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מכנסיים atone for גילוי עריות.

steps.title: The turban atones for arrogance, and the גמרא asks for the source
steps.stepSummary: The מצנפת atones for גסי הרוח. This time no פסוק is given, so the גמרא asks how we know this.
steps.simpleTranslation: The turban atones for the arrogant. From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The list states that the turban atones for arrogance. Then the גמרא asks for the source, which sets up רבי חנינא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now each garment came with a פסוק. Here none is given, so the גמרא wants to know what the match is based on.

keyTerms.meaning: the turban worn on the head

phrases.english: The turban atones for the arrogant.
From where do we know this?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִצְנֶפֶת מְכַפֶּרֶת עַל גַּסֵּי הָרוּחַ מִנַּיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next garment, but this time without a פסוק, so a source is requested.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The basis for linking the turban to arrogance.

steps.title: Something high atones for being high
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא explains that the turban sits high on the head, so it atones for a 'high', arrogant heart.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא said: Let something that is up high come and atone for haughtiness.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנינא answers the question from step 13 with a logical match instead of a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The turban is the highest garment, since it sits on top of the head. Arrogance is described as being 'high'. The match is based on height.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina said:
Let a thing that is up high come
and atone for haughtiness.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא יָבֹא דָּבָר שֶׁבַּגּוֹבַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The turban is worn high, so it atones for a haughty heart.

steps.title: The belt atones for sinful thoughts of the heart
steps.stepSummary: The אבנט atones for הרהור הלב, because it is worn at the place of the heart.
steps.simpleTranslation: The belt atones for thoughts of the heart, where it is located.
steps.whatsHappening: The list continues. The belt is matched to improper thoughts, and the reason is where it is worn.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'היכא דאיתיה' give the reason. The belt is wrapped around the body near the heart, so it atones for sins that happen in the heart.

keyTerms.meaning: thoughts of the heart, meaning sinful thoughts

phrases.english: The belt atones for thoughts of the heart,
where it is located.
phrases.notes: He means the belt sits right around the area of the heart.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבְנֵט מְכַפֵּר עַל הִרְהוּר הַלֵּב הֵיכָא דְּאִיתֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next garment, with a reason based on where it is worn.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The אבנט atones for הרהור הלב.

steps.title: The breastplate atones for wrong judgments
steps.stepSummary: The חושן atones for sins in judgment, because the Torah calls it the 'חושן משפט'.
steps.simpleTranslation: The breastplate atones for judgments, as it says: 'And you shall make a breastplate of judgment.'
steps.whatsHappening: The list continues with the כהן גדול's breastplate, which is matched to sins in judging.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah's own name for the breastplate includes the word משפט, judgment. Because of that name, it atones for corrupt or mistaken judgments.

keyTerms.meaning: the breastplate of the כהן גדול

phrases.english: The breastplate atones for judgments,
as it says: "And you shall make a breastplate of judgment."
phrases.notes: שמות 28:15.

steps.triggerLanguage: חוֹשֶׁן מְכַפֵּר עַל הַדִּינִין שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next garment on the list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חושן atones for sins in judgment.

steps.title: The ephod atones for idol worship
steps.stepSummary: The אפוד atones for עבודה זרה. The proof is a פסוק that mentions the אפוד together with תרפים, idols.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ephod atones for idol worship, as it says: 'Without ephod or teraphim.'
steps.whatsHappening: The list continues with the אפוד, which is matched to idol worship.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק puts the אפוד side by side with תרפים, which are idols. This pairing shows the אפוד is connected to the sin of idolatry, and so it atones for it.

keyTerms.meaning: the apron-like garment of the כהן גדול

phrases.english: The ephod atones for idol worship,
as it says: "Without ephod or teraphim."
phrases.notes: הושע 3:4.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵפוֹד מְכַפֵּר עַל עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next garment on the list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The אפוד atones for עבודה זרה.

steps.title: The robe atones for evil speech, and the גמרא asks for the source
steps.stepSummary: The מעיל atones for לשון הרע. No פסוק is given, so the גמרא asks how we know this.
steps.simpleTranslation: The robe atones for evil speech. From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The list says the robe atones for לשון הרע. Then the גמרא asks for the source, which sets up רבי חנינא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This works just like the turban in step 13. A garment is named without a פסוק, and the גמרא wants the basis for the match.

keyTerms.meaning: the robe of the כהן גדול

phrases.english: The robe atones for evil speech.
From where do we know this?

steps.triggerLanguage: מְעִיל מְכַפֵּר עַל לָשׁוֹן הָרָע מִנַּיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next garment, and like step 13 it has no פסוק, so a source is requested.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The basis for linking the robe to לשון הרע.

steps.title: Something that makes sound atones for evil sound
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא explains that the robe has bells that make sound, so it atones for the 'evil sound' of לשון הרע.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא said: Let something that makes sound come and atone for evil sound.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנינא answers the question from step 18, using the same kind of logic he used for the turban.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The robe had golden bells on its hem, which we saw in steps 6 and 7, so it makes noise when the כהן walks. לשון הרע is a sin of sound and speech. The match is based on sound.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina said:
Let a thing that makes sound come
phrases.notes: These are the robe's bells we learned about at the start of this discussion.

phrases.english: and atone for evil sound.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא יָבֹא דָּבָר שֶׁבַּקּוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The robe's bells make sound, so the robe atones for the evil sound of לשון הרע.

steps.title: The frontplate atones for brazenness
steps.stepSummary: The ציץ atones for עזות פנים. Both the ציץ and brazenness are described in פסוקים with the word מצח, forehead.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the frontplate atones for brazenness. About the frontplate it is written: 'And it shall be on אהרן's forehead.' And about brazenness it is written: 'And you had the forehead of a harlot.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last garment on the list. The ציץ is matched to brazen, shameless behavior by linking two פסוקים that share the word 'forehead'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ציץ is worn on the forehead. ירמיהו describes shameless behavior as having a 'harlot's forehead'. Because the same word appears in both פסוקים, the forehead-garment atones for the forehead-sin.

keyTerms.meaning: the golden frontplate of the כהן גדול

steps.whatToRemember: The eight garments each atone for a sin: כתונת for שפיכות דמים, מכנסיים for גילוי עריות, מצנפת for arrogance, אבנט for הרהור הלב, חושן for wrong judgments, אפוד for עבודה זרה, מעיל for לשון הרע, and ציץ for עזות פנים.

phrases.english: And the frontplate atones for brazenness;
about the frontplate it is written: "And it shall be on Aharon's forehead,"
phrases.notes: שמות 28:38.

phrases.english: and about brazenness it is written:
"And you had the forehead of a harlot."
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 3:3.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְצִיץ מְכַפֵּר עַל עַזּוּת פָּנִים בְּצִיץ כְּתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The final garment, which completes the list that began in step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ציץ atones for עזות פנים, shown by the shared word מצח.

steps.title: Is that so? רבי יהושע בן לוי says these two sins are atoned for in a different way
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the list of the בגדי כהונה. It quotes רבי יהושע בן לוי, who says שפיכות דמים and לשון הרע are not atoned for by קרבנות but by something else.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that really true? But רבי יהושע בן לוי said: there are two sins that we do not find atoned for with קרבנות, but we do find them atoned for in another way. They are שפיכות דמים and לשון הרע.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back against the list it just learned, where the בגדי כהונה atone for different sins. It brings a statement from רבי יהושע בן לוי that seems to clash with that list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier list linked the בגדי כהונה to sins, including שפיכות דמים (the כתונת, step 11) and לשון הרע (the מעיל, steps 18–19). רבי יהושע בן לוי says these two sins have a special 'other' atonement. The next steps spell out what that atonement is, and that will sharpen the clash.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that so? An opening word that signals a challenge
From another source, meaning something other than a קרבן

phrases.english: Is that so?!

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי:
phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi say:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁנֵי דְּבָרִים לֹא מָצִינוּ לָהֶן כַּפָּרָה בְּקׇרְבָּנוֹת,
phrases.english: Two things, we have not found atonement for them through offerings,
but we have found atonement for them from another place;

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵלּוּ הֵן: שְׁפִיכוּת דָּמִים וְלָשׁוֹן הָרָע!
phrases.english: and these are: bloodshed and evil speech!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינִי?! וְהָא אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the list of sins atoned for by the בגדי כהונה
steps.kashyaTarget: The list that matches each of the בגדי כהונה to a sin, especially שפיכות דמים and לשון הרע
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If these two sins have their own special atonement from 'another place', it seems clothing cannot be what atones for them.

steps.title: The other atonements: עגלה ערופה for bloodshed and קטרת for evil speech
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא names the 'other place': the עגלה ערופה atones for שפיכות דמים, and the קטרת atones for לשון הרע. רב חנניה's ברייתא proves from a פסוק that the קטרת atones.
steps.simpleTranslation: Bloodshed is atoned for by the עגלה ערופה, and לשון הרע by the קטרת. As רב חנניה taught: How do we know the קטרת atones? Because the פסוק says, 'And he put on the incense and atoned for the people.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what רבי יהושע בן לוי meant by 'another place.' It also brings a source showing that the קטרת can atone at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the challenge is concrete. Bloodshed has the עגלה ערופה and לשון הרע has the קטרת. רב חנניה's ברייתא proves the general point that קטרת atones, using the פסוק where אהרן stopped the plague with קטרת.

keyTerms.meaning: The calf whose neck is broken, brought when a murdered body is found
The incense offered in the בית המקדש

phrases.english: Bloodshed is atoned for by the heifer whose neck is broken,
phrases.notes: This is the calf brought when someone is found murdered and nobody knows who did it.

phrases.english: and evil speech by the incense.
As Rav Chananya taught:
From where do we know that incense atones?

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וַיִּתֵּן אֶת הַקְּטֹרֶת וַיְכַפֵּר עַל הָעָם״.
phrases.english: As it says: 'And he put on the incense and atoned for the people.'
phrases.notes: במדבר 17:12

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁפִיכוּת דָּמִים – מֵעֶגְלָה עֲרוּפָה, וְלָשׁוֹן הָרָע – מִקְּטֹרֶת. דְּתָנֵי רַב חֲנַנְיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the 'other place' in רבי יהושע בן לוי's statement and brings a source for it
steps.raayaObject: That the קטרת is an atonement

steps.title: דבי רבי ישמעאל: the private incense atones for private evil speech
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא from the school of רבי ישמעאל says the קטרת atones specifically for לשון הרע. Something done in private, the קטרת, atones for a sin done in private, לשון הרע.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught: For what does the קטרת atone? For לשון הרע. Let something done privately come and atone for an act done privately.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ברייתא showing that the קטרת's atonement is linked to לשון הרע in particular.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חנניה only proved that the קטרת atones in general. This ברייתא ties it to לשון הרע by a matching idea: the קטרת is offered quietly, and לשון הרע is usually said quietly, behind someone's back.

keyTerms.meaning: The school, or students, of רבי ישמעאל

phrases.english: And the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
For what does incense atone?
For evil speech.
Let a thing that is done in private come,
phrases.notes: The קטרת is offered quietly by one כהן, with nobody else present.

phrases.english: and atone for an act done in private.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתָנֵי דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל: עַל מָה קְטֹרֶת מְכַפֶּרֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second source that links the קטרת to לשון הרע specifically
steps.raayaObject: That the קטרת atones specifically for לשון הרע
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of דבי רבי ישמעאל, with the reasoning that private atones for private

steps.title: The double contradiction: evil speech against evil speech, bloodshed against bloodshed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא states the problem outright. The earlier list says the מעיל atones for לשון הרע, but here the קטרת does. The list says the כתונת atones for bloodshed, but here the עגלה ערופה does.
steps.simpleTranslation: So the statement about לשון הרע contradicts the other statement about לשון הרע, and the statement about bloodshed contradicts the other statement about bloodshed!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sums up the challenge as two clear contradictions. The answer will come in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each sin now has two different atonements claimed for it. For לשון הרע it is the מעיל or the קטרת. For bloodshed it is the כתונת or the עגלה ערופה. The גמרא needs to explain how both can be true.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a difficulty, a contradiction
Against, as in 'this one against that one'

steps.whatToRemember: Two sources contradict each other: the בגדי כהונה (the מעיל and the כתונת) versus the קטרת and the עגלה ערופה, for the same two sins.

phrases.english: There is a difficulty: evil speech against evil speech,
phrases.notes: Earlier the מעיל atoned for לשון הרע. Here the קטרת does, so the two statements clash.

phrases.english: there is a difficulty: bloodshed against bloodshed!
phrases.notes: The earlier list had the כתונת atoning for bloodshed. Here it is the עגלה ערופה.

steps.triggerLanguage: קַשְׁיָא לָשׁוֹן הָרָע אַלָּשׁוֹן הָרָע, קַשְׁיָא שְׁפִיכוּת דָּמִים אַשְּׁפִיכוּת דָּמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the sources in Steps 21 to 23 into an explicit contradiction with the list of the בגדי כהונה
steps.kashyaTarget: The claims that the מעיל atones for לשון הרע and the כתונת atones for bloodshed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Each of these sins has a different atonement assigned to it in the ברייתות (the קטרת and the עגלה ערופה), so the two sets of sources seem to conflict.

steps.title: Known killer versus unknown killer
steps.stepSummary: The כתונת atones for murder when we know who the killer is. The עגלה ערופה atones when we do not know who the killer is.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. This one, the כתונת, is when it is known who killed him. That one, the עגלה ערופה, is when it is not known who killed him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the first contradiction from step 24 by splitting murder into two different situations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sources talk about atonement for murder, but each one covers a different case. The עגלה ערופה is brought when a body is found and the killer is unknown. So the כתונת must cover the case where the killer is known.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult. This signals that an answer is coming.

phrases.english: It is not difficult;
this is where it is known who killed him,
phrases.notes: "This" is the כתונת from the list of בגדי כהונה.

phrases.english: that is where it is not known who killed him.
phrases.notes: "That" is the עגלה ערופה.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא; הָא דִּידִיעַ מַאן קַטְלֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the murder half of the contradiction raised in step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (each source covers a different case)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Two different things seemed to atone for the very same sin of murder.
steps.terutzMaskana: The כתונת covers a known killer, and the עגלה ערופה covers an unknown killer.

steps.title: A known killer should be executed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: if we know who the killer is, he should be put to death, so why would the כתונת be needed?
steps.simpleTranslation: If it is known who killed him, then that man deserves death!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer it just gave about a known killer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the killer is known, the normal outcome is that בית דין executes him. That seems to leave no room for the כתונת to be the thing that atones in that case. The answer from step 25 now looks shaky.

keyTerms.meaning: Someone who deserves to be put to death

phrases.english: If it is known who killed him –
he deserves to be put to death!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי דִּידִיעַ מַאן קַטְלֵיהּ – בַּר קְטָלָא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the 'known killer' case proposed in step 25.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 25 that the כתונת atones when the killer is known
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A known murderer is executed by בית דין, so the case seems to be dealt with through his death and not through the כתונת.

steps.title: He killed on purpose but was not warned
steps.stepSummary: The case is a killer who murdered on purpose, but no one gave him a warning beforehand, so בית דין cannot execute him.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is where he killed intentionally, but they did not warn him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends its answer by narrowing the case of the known killer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית דין can only execute a murderer who was warned before he acted. Here we know who did it and that he did it on purpose, but there was no warning, so he cannot be executed. That is the case where the כתונת atones.

keyTerms.meaning: A warning given before a sin. It is needed before בית דין can punish.

steps.whatToRemember: Murder: the כתונת atones when the killer is known (he acted on purpose but was not warned). The עגלה ערופה atones when the killer is unknown.

phrases.english: Intentionally
and they did not warn him.
phrases.notes: Without a warning, בית דין cannot put him to death.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמֵזִיד וְלָא אַתְרוֹ בֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection in step 26.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A known killer is always executed, so the כתונת has no role.
steps.terutzMaskana: The case is a killer who acted on purpose without a warning. He cannot be executed, so the כתונת atones.

steps.title: Private gossip versus public gossip
steps.stepSummary: The קטרת atones for לשון הרע spoken in private, and the מעיל atones for לשון הרע spoken in public.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the contradiction between one source on לשון הרע and the other source on לשון הרע is also not difficult. This one is in private, and that one is in public.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the second contradiction from step 24, about לשון הרע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Again, each source covers a different case. The קטרת, which is offered in private, atones for gossip spoken in private, just as step 23 taught. The מעיל atones for gossip spoken in public.
steps.whatToRemember: לשון הרע: the קטרת atones for private gossip, and the מעיל atones for public gossip.

phrases.english: And the contradiction of evil speech against evil speech
phrases.notes: He means the list's מעיל against the קטרת, since both were said to atone for לשון הרע.

phrases.english: is also not difficult –
this is in private,
phrases.notes: "This" is the קטרת, matching the private-for-private idea from step 23.

phrases.english: that is in public.
phrases.notes: "That" is the מעיל.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָשׁוֹן הָרָע אַלָּשׁוֹן הָרָע נָמֵי לָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallels step 25, now answering the לשון הרע half of the contradiction from step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (each source covers a different case)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both the מעיל and the קטרת seemed to atone for the same sin of לשון הרע.
steps.terutzMaskana: The קטרת covers private לשון הרע, and the מעיל covers public לשון הרע.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing פרק המזבח מקדש
steps.stepSummary: The closing line of the פרק called המזבח מקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, המזבח מקדש.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the traditional line said at the end of a פרק. It closes פרק המזבח מקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן is not part of the argument. It marks that the פרק is finished and expresses the hope of coming back to learn it again.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you. This is said when finishing a פרק.
The name of the פרק being closed: the altar sanctifies

phrases.english: We will return to you, "The altar sanctifies"

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲדַרַן עֲלָךְ הַמִּזְבֵּחַ מְקַדֵּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the פרק after the final answer in step 28.
